### cylinder2d {#sec-example-laminar-cylinder2d}

This example examines a steady flow past a cylinder placed in a channel.
The cylinder is offset somewhat from the center of the flow to make the steady-state symmetrical flow unstable.
At the inlet, a Poiseuille profile is imposed on the velocity, whereas the outlet implements a Dirichlet pressure condition set by $p = 0$, inspired by [@turek:96].
For high resolution, low `latticeU`, and enough time to converge, the results for pressure drop, drag, and lift lie within the estimated intervals for the exact results.
An unsteady flow with Kármán vortex street can be created by changing the Reynolds number to $Re=100$.

#### Governing equations

The domain $\Omega \times \I \subseteq [0, 2.2] \times [0, 0.41] \times \R_{\geq 0}$, the channel without the cylinder, is considered with the following governing equations with the velocity field $\vel \in \R^2$ and the pressure $p \in \R$ for the incompressible flow of a Newtonian fluid with kinematic viscosity $\nu \in \R_{> 0}$ and constant density $\rho \in \R_{> 0}$,
\begin{align}
    \nabla \cdot \vel &= 0 \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I, \\
    \partial_t \vel + (\vel \cdot \nabla) \vel &= -\frac{1}{\rho} \nabla p + \nu \Delta \vel \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I.
\end{align}

#### Boundary conditions

The boundary $\partial \Omega = \Gamma_D \cup \Gamma_\text{out} \cup \Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$ consists of three parts (@fig-cylinder2d-domain): the inlet $\Gamma_D$ on the left, where a parabolic velocity profile is prescribed as a Dirichlet condition, the outlet $\Gamma_\text{out}$ on the right, where the pressure is prescribed, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$, which comprises the two channel walls and the surface of the cylinder,
\begin{align}
    \vel &= (u_\text{in}(y, t), 0)^\top \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_D \times \I, \\
    p &= 0 \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_\text{out} \times \I, \\
    \vel &= \mathbf{0} \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}} \times \I.
\end{align}
The inflow profile
$$
    u_\text{in}(y, t) = s(t)\, \frac{4\, U_\text{max}\, y (H - y)}{H^2}
$$
with the peak velocity $U_\text{max} = \tfrac{3}{2} U$ has the mean velocity $U$ once it is fully developed.
`setTemporalValues()` raises it smoothly from rest, with a polynomial ramp $s(t)$ that grows from $0$ to $1$ during the first $40\,\%$ of the simulated time and is updated every $0.01\,\mathrm{s}$.
The fluid is initially at rest, $\vel = \mathbf{0}$ in $\Omega$ at $t = 0$.

#### Domain

The channel has the length $L = 2.2\,\mathrm{m}$ and the height $H = 0.41\,\mathrm{m}$ (@fig-cylinder2d-domain).
The cylinder with the diameter $D = 0.1\,\mathrm{m}$ sits at $(0.2\,\mathrm{m}, 0.2\,\mathrm{m})$, slightly below the centre line, which makes the flow asymmetric and gives a lift.
With the mean inflow velocity $U = 0.2\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and $\nu = 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^2/s}$, the Reynolds number is $Re = U D / \nu = 20$, and the flow becomes steady.

`prepareGeometry()` assigns the material numbers (MN) shown in @fig-cylinder2d-domain.

![Domain and boundary conditions of `cylinder2d`, with the material numbers (MN) assigned in `prepareGeometry()`.](/examples/laminar/cylinder2d/doc/fig/cylinder2dDomain.svg){width="100%" #fig-cylinder2d-domain .lightbox}

#### Discretization \& Descriptor
In this example, the domain is discretized with a uniform grid with the lattice spacing $\Delta x = D / N$, where $N = 10$ cells resolve the diameter of the cylinder.

The LBM collision operator is the BGK operator with a single relaxation time ([Collision Operators](/content/02_core.qmd#collision-operators)), used as `BGKdynamics`, together with the D2Q9 velocity set ([Lattice Structures](/content/01_introduction.qmd#sec-lattice-structures)).
The boundaries are treated as follows ([Define Boundary Method](/content/06_initial_boundary.qmd#sec-defineBoundaryMethod)):

- the channel walls (MN 2) with `BounceBack`,
- the inlet (MN 3) with `InterpolatedVelocity`,
- the outlet (MN 4) with `InterpolatedPressure`,
- the cylinder (MN 5) with the Bouzidi boundary, `setBouzidiBoundary()`, which takes the exact position of the curved surface between the lattice nodes into account. Without the `BOUZIDI` define in `case.h`, the cylinder falls back to `BounceBack`.

The corresponding lattice is defined inside the case definition in `case.h` as in @lst-cylinder2d-case.

::: {#lst-cylinder2d-case}
```{.cpp}
using MyCase = Case<
  NavierStokes, Lattice<FLOATING_POINT_TYPE, descriptors::D2Q9<>>
>;
```
Case definition for the `cylinder2d` example.
:::

The parameters for the simulation are set in `main()` and given in @tbl-cylinder2d-params.
The unit converter is built from them and derives the time step size from the resolution and the lattice relaxation time.

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RESOLUTION` | $N$ | $10$ | cells per cylinder diameter $D$ |
| `REYNOLDS` | $Re$ | $20$ | Reynolds number $U D / \nu$ |
| `PHYS_MAX_T` | $T$ | $16\,\mathrm{s}$ | simulated time, $8\,000$ time steps |
| `DOMAIN_EXTENT` | $L \times H$ | $2.2\,\mathrm{m} \times 0.41\,\mathrm{m}$ | length and height of the channel |
| `PHYS_CHAR_VELOCITY` | $U$ | $0.2\,\mathrm{m/s}$ | mean velocity of the fully developed inflow |
| `LATTICE_RELAXATION_TIME` | $\tau$ | $0.56$ | lattice relaxation time |
| `PHYS_CHAR_DENSITY` | $\rho$ | $1\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ | density |
| `RADIUS_CYLINDER` | $D/2$ | $0.05\,\mathrm{m}$ | radius of the cylinder |
| `CENTER_CYLINDER` | | $(0.2\,\mathrm{m}, 0.2\,\mathrm{m})$ | centre of the cylinder |
| `PHYS_CHAR_LENGTH` | $D$ | $0.1\,\mathrm{m}$ | characteristic length, derived as $2 \cdot$ `RADIUS_CYLINDER` |
| `PHYS_CHAR_VISCOSITY` | $\nu$ | $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^2/s}$ | kinematic viscosity, derived as $D U / Re$ |
| `PHYS_VTK_ITER_T` | | $0.3\,\mathrm{s}$ | interval of the VTK output and the heat maps |
| `PHYS_STAT_ITER_T` | | $0.1\,\mathrm{s}$ | interval of the console statistics and of drag, lift and pressure drop |
| `RAMP_UP_UPDATE` | | $0.01\,\mathrm{s}$ | interval at which the inflow is updated during the ramp-up |
| `RAMP_UP_END_FRACTION` | | $0.4$ | fraction of $T$ after which the inflow is fully developed |

: Parameters of `cylinder2d`, as set in `main()`. Each of them can be overridden on the command line, e.g. `./cylinder2d --RESOLUTION 20`. {#tbl-cylinder2d-params}

#### Validation

The velocity and the pressure are written in physical units every $0.3\,\mathrm{s}$.
@fig-cylinder2d-velocity shows the velocity magnitude at the end of the simulation: the flow accelerates around the cylinder, and a closed recirculation region forms in its wake.

![Magnitude of the physical velocity of `cylinder2d` at $t = 15.9\,\mathrm{s}$, with the default resolution $N = 10$, visualized in ParaView.](/examples/laminar/cylinder2d/doc/fig/cylinder2d_velocity.png){width="100%" #fig-cylinder2d-velocity .lightbox}

The example reproduces the steady test case 2D-1 of @turek:96.
Every $0.1\,\mathrm{s}$, `getResults()` evaluates the drag and lift coefficients of the cylinder,
$$
    c_D = \frac{2 F_D}{\rho U^2 D}, \qquad c_L = \frac{2 F_L}{\rho U^2 D},
$$
where $F_D$ and $F_L$ are the forces on the cylinder in and across the flow direction, and the pressure drop $\Delta p = p(x_a) - p(x_e)$ between the front and the back of the cylinder, $x_a = (0.15\,\mathrm{m}, 0.2\,\mathrm{m})$ and $x_e = (0.25\,\mathrm{m}, 0.2\,\mathrm{m})$.
It prints them to the console and writes the drag over time to `tmp/gnuplotData/`, together with the reference value $c_D = 5.58$.

@tbl-cylinder2d-validation compares the values at the end of the simulation with the intervals that @turek:96 give for the exact solution.
With the default resolution $N = 10$, which keeps the run short, drag and pressure drop deviate by about $4\,\%$ from the reference and the lift by about $40\,\%$, and the drag has not quite settled at the end of the run. Refining the grid brings all three values to the reference: with $N = 40$ they lie within half a percent of the upper bounds of the reference intervals.
@fig-cylinder2d-drag shows the drag coefficient over time for the three resolutions.

| Resolution $N$ | $c_D$ | $c_L$ | $\Delta p$ [Pa] |
|---|---|---|---|
| $10$ (default) | $5.821$ | $0.0153$ | $0.1225$ |
| $20$ | $5.632$ | $0.0122$ | $0.1184$ |
| $40$ | $5.591$ | $0.0111$ | $0.1180$ |
| reference [@turek:96] | $5.57$ – $5.59$ | $0.0104$ – $0.0110$ | $0.1172$ – $0.1176$ |

: Drag coefficient, lift coefficient and pressure drop of `cylinder2d` at $t = 15.9\,\mathrm{s}$ for increasing resolution, run with `--RESOLUTION`, compared with the reference intervals of the test case 2D-1. {#tbl-cylinder2d-validation}

![Drag coefficient $c_D$ of `cylinder2d` over time for the resolutions $N = 10$, $20$ and $40$, and the reference value $c_D = 5.58$. The drag rises while the inflow is ramped up during the first $6.4\,\mathrm{s}$ and then settles.](/examples/laminar/cylinder2d/doc/fig/drag/drag.svg){width="80%" #fig-cylinder2d-drag .lightbox}

#### Files

```
cylinder2d/
├── cylinder2d.cpp   main(): parameters, then mesh, geometry, lattice, initial values and time loop
├── case.h           Case type, geometry, boundary conditions, inflow ramp-up, drag, lift and pressure drop
└── Makefile
```

The results are written to `tmp/` in the directory the example is run from: `vtkData/cylinder2d.pvd` opens all time steps in ParaView, `imageData/` holds the velocity heat maps and `gnuplotData/` the drag over time. Both the heat maps and the drag plot are drawn with gnuplot; without it, only the data in `gnuplotData/data/` is written.
